title: Springs and Hooke's law
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D06-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; D06-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D06-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; D06-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D06-1#N.2a, D06-1#N.4b, D06-1#N.11, D06-1#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Natural length
items.clue: Original, unstretched size of a spring from end to end.

items.label: Extension
items.clue: Stretched length minus the original length, not the whole length.

items.label: Compression
items.clue: Squashing a spring, where the change counted is the decrease in length.

items.label: Hooke's law
items.clue: Statement that the pull of a spring is proportional to how far it has been stretched.

questions.stem: An ideal spring has a relaxed length of 10 cm. When it is stretched to a length of 14 cm, it exerts a force of magnitude 3.0 N on the object attached to it. What is the magnitude of the force it exerts when it is stretched to a length of 22 cm?

A block on a level surface with negligible friction is attached to two identical ideal springs; the other end of each spring is fixed to a wall, one on each side of the block. When the block is at its equilibrium position, both springs have their relaxed lengths. The block is pulled a distance d to the right and released from rest. Which statement describes the forces exerted on the block by the two springs just after it is released?

options.text: They point in opposite directions and add up to zero.
Both point to the left, toward the block's equilibrium position.
Both point to the right, the direction of the displacement.
Both are zero, as the block is at rest at that instant.

questions.stem: Two ideal springs, of spring constants 300 N/m and 600 N/m, are joined end to end. One free end is held fixed, and a 12 N force is exerted on the other free end along the springs. By how much does the pair stretch in total?
A spring that obeys Hooke's law is 15.0 cm long when it supports a 3.0 N load and 18.0 cm long when it supports a 6.0 N load. What is its natural (unloaded) length?
questions.explanation: The extra 3.0 N adds 3.0 cm, so the extension is 1.0 cm per newton. With 3.0 N on, the extension is 3.0 cm: natural length = 15.0 − 3.0 = 12.0 cm.
